decisions.decision: Shopper read multipliers (x10 browse, x5 detail, x3 history per order) and a demo peak of ~1 order/s are accepted for sizing.
Product search (CAT-12): case-insensitive name-prefix in DynamoDB for the demo; OpenSearch (zero-ETL) later.
Carts (SAL-01) only for logged-in customers (cartId = customerId); items expire via TTL after 7 days.
The .NET 10 app writes orders directly to DynamoDB; the old app keeps writing SQL, which flows one-way via CDC (side-by-side cutover).
DynamoDB-created orders get ids from a range above SQL's, with a source prefix on the order number.
Phase 3 key design covers all 7 domains, including back-office patterns.
Territory and sales-person lists (SAL-08, SAL-09, CUS-10) are served by Redshift only.
Strong consistency only for login (CUS-01), cart (SAL-01) and read-after-checkout (SAL-04 right after SAL-02); everything else eventual.
Product descriptions kept in all 6 cultures (CAT-13).
SQL deletes become tombstone items in DynamoDB (TTL later) so Redshift sees deletes (CDC-02).

legend.scope: dynamodb = must be served by domain table keys (phase 3); redshift = served by zero-ETL/Redshift, no keys; opensearch-or-defer; out-of-scope
legend.frequency: estimated from AdventureWorks2022 row counts (orders 2011-05-31..2014-06-30 = 31,465 orders ≈ 28/day; 27,659 online) plus demo bursts

domains.name: Catalog
domains.summary: Everything a shopper browses: categories, products, models, descriptions, photos, reviews, price history and offers. Read-dominated (browse/detail pages) with rare admin writes; must serve the shopper pages with one request per page.

domains.name: Inventory & Manufacturing
domains.summary: Stock per location, inventory movements, bills of materials and work orders. Write-heavy back-office data; only 'is it in stock' reaches the shopper, as a pre-aggregated copy on the product.

domains.name: Sales
domains.summary: Carts, checkout, orders and lines, and the sales organisation (sales people, quotas, territories). Hot path of the live demo: the order a test customer places flows SQL -> CDC -> DynamoDB here.

domains.name: Customer & Party
domains.summary: Identity and profile: persons, stores, logins, emails, phones, addresses, payment cards, store contacts. Serves login, checkout address/card selection and the customer screens.

domains.name: Purchasing
domains.summary: Vendors, which products they supply, and purchase orders. Low volume back-office workload.

domains.name: HR
domains.summary: Employees, departments, shifts, pay history, org chart, candidates. Small but sensitive; isolated table and IAM.

domains.name: Reference
domains.summary: Shared lookups: countries, states, currencies and FX rates, tax rates, ship methods, units, cultures. Read-mostly, cached by apps and copied into other domains' items.

domains.name: Cross-cutting
domains.summary: Patterns every domain must support for replication and analytics: idempotent CDC upserts/deletes and the zero-ETL feed to Redshift.

patterns.question: Which products are below their reorder point / safety stock?

hard.approach: Sparse 'needs reorder' marker maintained when stock changes (written by the same stream that updates totals); or Redshift report.

patterns.question: Record a stock movement and list movements for a product over a date range
patterns.notes: In SQL the order-detail trigger writes a TransactionHistory row per order line; in the target this becomes an event from Sales, not a cross-table write.

patterns.question: Explode the bill of materials for an assembly (all levels, as of a date)

hard.approach: Store BOM edges per assembly; app iterates levels (max depth ~4, 2,679 edges) or keep a materialized flattened tree per top-level assembly, rebuilt on change.

patterns.question: Where is this component used?

hard.approach: Inverted index on BOM edges (component -> assembly), iterate levels in app.

patterns.question: Which work orders are open / due, and what are a work order's routing steps?
patterns.result: work orders by due date; one WO with routings

patterns.question: Daily inventory balance per product (history)

hard.approach: Redshift: rebuild from zero-ETL'd transaction history (phase 6). No DynamoDB keys.

patterns.question: Add / change / remove an item in my cart, and show my cart
patterns.inputs: cartId (= customer or anonymous session), productId, qty
patterns.result: cart lines with current product name/price
patterns.notes: Logged-in customers only, cartId = customerId; 7-day TTL (D3). Only 3 rows today. Product name/price read from Catalog at render time.

patterns.question: Check out: turn my cart into an order (header + lines) with tax, freight, totals
patterns.inputs: customerId, cart, ship-to/bill-to address, ship method, card
patterns.notes: Needs product price/offer (CAT-10), tax rate (REF-02), ship method (REF-04), address/card snapshot (CUS-03). Header SubTotal maintained in the same transaction (replaces trigger). Max 72 lines/order today. The .NET 10 app writes orders directly to DynamoDB; the old app writes SQL and flows via CDC (one-way, side-by-side cutover) (D4). DynamoDB-created orders get ids from a range above SQL's with a source prefix (D5).

Apply a source change (insert/update) to the target item(s), idempotently, keyed by the SQL primary key
patterns.inputs: source table, source PK, after-image, LSN/commit ts
patterns.frequency: every OLTP write (68 tables); demo bursts
patterns.notes: Requires every target item to be addressable from its source PK (deterministic key) and to carry the last-applied LSN.

patterns.question: Apply a source delete
patterns.notes: DECIDED (D10): SQL deletes become tombstone items (deleted flag, TTL later) so zero-ETL/Redshift sees the delete; e.g. reset-demo deletes demo orders.

patterns.question: Fan out a source change to denormalized copies in other items/domains
patterns.result: copies refreshed (e.g. product name on catalog listings, person name on employee)

hard.approach: Event-driven refresh via DynamoDB Streams/EventBridge; immutable snapshots (order lines, order addresses) are never refreshed.

patterns.question: Child row arrives before its parent (e.g. order line before header)
patterns.result: item written without waiting for parent
patterns.notes: Design keys so a child can be written using only its own source columns (no lookup of the parent required).

patterns.question: Land all domain data in Redshift continuously
patterns.notes: Needs entityType + plain-named business attributes on every item (not only inside PK/SK).
